title: The adjunct of a strict compatible family is its normalized Roos lift
statement: For a prime l, finite extension E of Q_l and scheme X, let rho be a normalized Roos comparison [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. For any completed-coefficient complex P, strict tower complex C and chain map b from the constant tower on P to C, the derived constant/limit adjunct of Q(b), preceded by the exact constant-functor comparison, followed by rho at C equals Q of the ordinary constant/limit adjunct of b followed by the specified limit-to-Roos inclusion. No K-flatness or boundedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0941, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok and the preceding constant/limit adjunction discussion in section-derived-limits; agent expansion of scalar-model-unit proof step 3.

proof.text: Transpose b through the ordinary constant/limit adjunction. The proved derived_transpose_ordinary formula identifies the derived adjunct with the localization of this ordinary adjunct followed by the universal right-derived limit unit.
The defining coordinates of integralComparisonLimitToRoos and the two coordinate formulas for the Roos map prove naturality of the ordinary inclusion, by product and biproduct extensionality.

On K-injective towers rho.computes and rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ_eq cancel the inverse comparison with its hom. Choose a simultaneous K-injective resolution of C. Naturality transports this equality to C after cancellation of the Roos map, which is invertible after localization by naturality of rho. Compose with the localized ordinary adjunct.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0941; formal naturality expansion of lem-trf-scalar-model-unit step 3.

mathlib_searches.query: The adjoint of a strict map from a constant tower to a tower of complexes is the map into the Roos cone with zero shifted coordinate
mathlib_searches.results: The returned mapping-cone comparison lemmas do not compute the normalized derived-limit adjunct.
Found CategoryTheory.Limits.constLimAdj in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasLimits; it supplies the ordinary adjunction but no Roos comparison.

theorem integralComparisonRoosTranspose
    (ρ : IntegralComparisonRoosModel l E X)
    (P : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E X) ℤ)
    (C : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E X) ℤ)
    (b : ((Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : scalarReductionSource l E X ⥤
      ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P ⟶ C) :
    (integralComparisonConstantAdjunction l E X).homEquiv _ _
        ((Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : scalarReductionSource l E X ⥤
          ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E X).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P ≫
          DerivedCategory.Q.map b) ≫ ρ.comparison.hom.app C =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map
        (((constLimAdj (J := ℕᵒᵖ) (C := scalarReductionSource l E X)).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).homEquiv P C b ≫ integralComparisonLimitToRoos l E X C)
